title: 1972 BMW 2002
subtitle: Inka Orange
summary: Round tails, a black grille swap and the stance it always deserved.
thesis: The small sedan that taught America what a sports sedan could be. Light, simple, rear wheel drive, with a parts world that never went away. This build keeps the round taillights and borrows the later black grille, then fixes the stance.

photo.alt: 1972 BMW 2002 in Inka Orange with round taillights, black grille and lowered stance

parts.name: Black Grille Set
parts.note: The signature move. The later black center and side grilles on an early round tail car. Bolt on, one evening, and the face changes completely.

parts.name: Sport Shocks and Springs
parts.note: A matched set of sport shocks and lowering springs takes out the factory ride height and body roll while keeping the car comfortable enough to drive daily.

parts.name: 13 in Wheels and Tires
parts.note: Period size, modern rubber. A 13 in wheel with a wider, stickier tire fills the arches without rubbing once the springs are in.

parts.name: Sway Bar Kit
parts.note: Thicker front and rear bars flatten the car in corners. The cheapest real handling upgrade an '02 can get.

parts.name: Sport Steering Wheel
parts.note: A smaller, thicker wheel with a hub adapter. The thing your hands touch every drive.

bundle.name: Starter Build
bundle.pitch: New to old BMWs? The three changes that deliver most of the look and feel, in install order.

detailing.note: Wash, then clay the paint. Fifty year old single stage paint holds grime the mitt leaves behind.
Single stage paint polishes back to color fast. Expect orange on the pad; that's normal. Go gentle.
Seal the paint and polish the chrome bumpers. Ten minutes for months of shine.
